title: Soreng month by month: when to go
meta_description: Soreng weather and travel month by month: rhododendrons at Barsey, clear Kangchenjunga views, monsoon roads, festivals and which months to avoid.
summary: The best months for Soreng are March and April for rhododendrons at Barsey and October to December for clear Kangchenjunga views from Rinchenpong and Kaluk. January and February are cold but bright. June to September is the monsoon, with rain, leeches and landslides. May is warm and hazy but still good for the higher flowers.

sections.heading: The year at a glance
paras: Soreng's villages sit between about 500 m and 2,600 m, with the Barsey sanctuary above, so the weather changes as much with altitude as with the month. The figures below are typical ranges for Rinchenpong and Kaluk at about 1,700 m; Okhrey at about 2,200 m is 3–4 °C colder, and Hilley and Barsey colder still. Rainfall averages about 1,600 mm a year according to the district administration, most of it between June and September. Ratings are ours: 2 is best, 1 is good, 0 is best avoided.

sections.heading: Winter: December to February
paras: Winter is the season of long, clear mornings. From the Rinchenpong and Kaluk ridge the Kangchenjunga range is usually out from dawn until late morning, and the light is sharp all day. Days are pleasant in the sun, around 12–15 °C at Rinchenpong, but nights drop to about 3–5 °C, colder in Okhrey and close to freezing at Hilley. Few homestays have heating, so bring a down jacket, thermals, a warm hat and socks for the evenings.

December is lively in Limbu villages, with Chasok Tangnam, the harvest festival, observed as a state holiday on 15 December in recent lists, and Teyongsi Sirijunga Sawan Tongnam later in the month. In January, Maghe Sankranti around 14 January brings the large Maghe Mela fair beside the Rangeet at Jorethang, on the way into the district. Snow can fall at Hilley and Barsey in January and February; the walk is lovely in fresh snow but icy, and the Hilley road occasionally shuts for a day or two. Losar, the Tibetan and Sherpa new year, falls in February or early March and is celebrated in Okhrey and other Buddhist villages.

sections.heading: Spring: March to May
paras: Spring is Soreng's famous season. Tree rhododendrons start flowering on the lower slopes around Okhrey from late February, and the colour climbs the hill week by week. The Hilley to Barsey trail is usually at its best from the last week of March to the last week of April, with reds, pinks and whites together; higher species carry on into May. A late frost or a dry winter can shift the peak by up to two weeks, so we check with homestays in Okhrey before fixing dates.

Days are mild and walking weather is ideal, around 18–22 °C at Rinchenpong. The trade-off is haze: mountain views are less reliable than in autumn, with the best chance at dawn. April is the busiest month of the year in Okhrey and Hilley, especially at weekends and around the Bengali new year in mid-April; book homestays a month ahead. By May the air is warmer and hazier, and pre-monsoon storms can bring afternoon thunder and hail.

sections.heading: Monsoon: June to September
paras: The south-west monsoon usually reaches Sikkim in early June and brings most of the year's rain by the end of September. Days are warm and humid, cloud hides the mountains most of the time, and forest trails, including the Barsey walk, are full of leeches. The bigger issue is the road. NH10 along the Teesta closes after landslides most monsoons, and smaller roads inside the district can be cut for hours or days. The alternative into Soreng is via Darjeeling down to Jorethang.

If you do come in the monsoon, travel with spare days, keep plans loose and stay in one place. The villages are at their greenest, homestays are cheapest and you will have them almost to yourself. Late September is often a good gamble, as the rain eases and the first clear mornings return. Pang Lhabsol, the festival honouring Kangchenjunga as Sikkim's guardian deity, falls in August or September and is marked across the state.

sections.heading: Autumn: October and November
paras: Autumn is the other peak season, and for mountain views it is the best. The air is washed clean by the monsoon, the farms are green and gold, and from mid-October the Kangchenjunga range is visible for most of the morning on most days. Temperatures are comfortable, around 17–20 °C by day at Rinchenpong, with cool nights. The Barsey walk has no flowers now but has the clearest views of the year from the top.

The catch is the holiday calendar. Durga Puja and Dasain, then Diwali and Tihar, fall in October or November and fill hotels and homestays across Sikkim, mostly with travellers from West Bengal. Book a month or more ahead for those weeks, or come in the first days of October or the second half of November, when rooms are easier and rates lower.

sections.heading: Each month in one line
paras: A quick note for each month, from the questions guests ask us most. Use it with the table at the top of this guide. Remember that the higher you go, the later spring arrives and the earlier winter comes: Hilley and Barsey run two to three weeks behind Rinchenpong for flowers.
list: January: brightest mornings of the year, cold nights, possible snow at Hilley; bring real winter clothes
February: still cold, very quiet, Losar in some years; the first red tree rhododendrons appear low down
March: rhododendrons climb towards Hilley through the month; mild days and good walking
April: peak bloom on the Hilley to Barsey trail and the busiest homestays; book a month ahead
May: higher species still flowering, warm days, haze and afternoon storms
June: monsoon arrives; quiet, cheap and green, but leeches and road risk start
July: wettest month; only for travellers with flexible plans
August: heavy rain continues; Pang Lhabsol may fall late in the month
September: rain eases towards the end; first clear mornings return
October: views come back and farms are green and gold; festival holidays fill rooms
November: clearest and steadiest weather; our favourite month for the ridge
December: clear and cold; Limbu festivals and the start of the orange harvest

sections.heading: Choosing a month for your trip
list: Rhododendrons at Barsey: last week of March to last week of April
Clear Kangchenjunga views: mid-October to mid-December
Fewest visitors with good weather: late February, early October, late November
Families with school holidays: October and December, booked early
Lowest prices: June to September, with weather and road risk
Snow at Hilley: January and February, not guaranteed
paras: Whatever month you choose, Soreng's weather can change within an hour. Pack layers and a rain jacket in every season, start walks early, and keep one spare day on longer trips. Festival dates and road conditions change every year, so check current status before you travel.

Prices follow the seasons too. Homestay and hotel rates are highest in April and during the October and December holiday weeks, and lowest from June to September. Cars cost about the same all year, but drivers are scarce in the peak weeks, so book them with your rooms. If you are flexible, the cheapest good-weather window is usually the second half of November.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Soreng?
faqs.a: April is best for rhododendrons, with the Hilley to Barsey trail usually peaking from the last week of March to the last week of April. November is best for clear, steady weather and Kangchenjunga views from Rinchenpong and Kaluk. March, October and December are also very good. Avoid June to August, when monsoon rain, leeches and landslides are common.

faqs.q: When do rhododendrons bloom at Barsey?
faqs.a: Usually from March to May, with the peak on the Hilley to Barsey trail between the last week of March and the last week of April. Tree rhododendrons flower first on the lower slopes from late February, and higher species continue into May. Weather can shift the peak by up to two weeks, so check a bloom report before fixing dates.

Not in the main villages. Rinchenpong, Kaluk and Soreng bazaar get cold winter nights of about 3–5 °C but rarely snow. Hilley, at about 2,730 m, and Barsey, at about 3,000 m, can get snow in January and February, and Okhrey occasionally sees a light fall. Snow is never guaranteed, and the Hilley road may close for a day after heavy falls.

faqs.q: Is it safe to visit Soreng in the monsoon?
faqs.a: It is possible but needs flexibility. From June to September heavy rain causes landslides that can close NH10 and smaller roads for hours or days, cloud hides the mountains, and forest trails have leeches. If you go, keep spare days, stay in one place, follow local advice and check current status before you travel. Late September is often better.

faqs.q: How cold is Rinchenpong in December?
faqs.a: Days are pleasant in the sun, around 13–15 °C, but nights fall to about 4–6 °C, and colder when the wind blows along the ridge. Most homestays and small hotels have no heating, so bring a down jacket, thermals, a warm hat and socks. Okhrey is a few degrees colder, and Hilley and Barsey colder still.

faqs.q: When can I see Kangchenjunga from Soreng?
faqs.a: Most reliably from mid-October to mid-December, when the air is clear and the range is visible for most mornings. January to March is also good, especially at sunrise. In April and May haze often softens or hides the peaks after early morning, and from June to September cloud covers them most days.

faqs.q: Is April too crowded in Okhrey?
faqs.a: April weekends are busy in Okhrey and on the Hilley to Barsey trail, especially around mid-April holidays, and homestays fill up a month ahead. Weekdays are calmer. Start the walk by 7–8 am to beat the crowds and the clouds. Late March, or the last days of April, often have good flowers with fewer people.

Limbu villages celebrate Chasok Tangnam, the harvest festival, in December, and Sikkim marks Teyongsi Sirijunga Sawan Tongnam later that month. Losar, the Tibetan and Sherpa new year, falls in February or March in Buddhist villages such as Okhrey. Dasain and Tihar in October and November are celebrated everywhere. Dates change, so check current status.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Soreng in spring?
faqs.a: Layers: a fleece or light down jacket for mornings and evenings, a rain jacket for afternoon showers, comfortable walking shoes with grip for the Barsey trail, a sun hat and sunscreen, and a refillable water bottle. Nights in Okhrey can still fall to about 5 °C in April, so a warm layer for sleeping helps.
